evidence: Nestled discreetly between the bustling streets of Hàng Lược and Hàng Mã, Hang Ruoi Street stands out as a quaint and serene passage within the vibrant tapestry of Hanoi’s historic district. Historically, this narrow thoroughfare served as a vital trading hub during the autumn season when merchants transported rươi, a prized delicacy from the Chiêm Trũng region, to the bustling capital city of Kinh Kỳ.

During the festive period leading up to Tết, the street transforms into a lively market, blending seamlessly with the nearby traditional flower market, where visitors can immerse themselves in the rich cultural traditions of Vietnamese New Year celebrations. The ambiance of Hang Ruoi Street is further enriched by the presence of street food vendors offering a variety of rustic dishes, adding to the sensory experience of those who wander through its narrow pathways.
